name: Monk of Montaudon
bio: The Monk of Montaudon came from Auvergne, was made a monk of the abbey of Orllac, and was given the priory of Montaudon. Farnell's Life says that he made coblas and sirventes while still in the monastery.

The verse in this selection is Ida Farnell's English version in The Lives of the Troubadours (London: David Nutt, 1896), where it stands beside a prose Life of the poet; the prose Life is not reproduced here. The dates are those Farnell prints for the period in which the poet was active, and the Old Occitan original is not included.

poems.title: The Monk of Montaldon's Vision of Heaven
poems.author: Monk of Montaudon
poems.text:
Whilom I did Heaven see,
Whence I'm glad and free of care;
Loving greeting gave me there
God, who rules all things that be.
Earth and ocean, mountain, valley:
"Monk, why cam'st thou here?" spake he,
"How does my Montaldon fare,
Where thy friends around thee rally?"

"Lord, for well-nigh two years' space
'Neath the cloisters' yoke I've lain.
Whence the barons me disdain,
And will turn from me their face.
E'en that here I sing thy praises;
Randon, who was never base,
Who o'er Paris has his reign
Lamentation for me raises."

"Monk, 'tis evil in my sight,
That 'twixt convent walls thou art,
And on strife dost set thy heart,
Eager for dispute and fight,
For thy rule 'gainst neighbours striving;
Songs I love and laughter bright,
These great worth to life impart,
Montaldon through them is thriving.

"Lord, I feared to go astray
If to singing I inclined:
Who delight in lies does find.
In thy favour cannot stay,
Singing then I have forsaken.
From the world have turned away,
On the lessons set my mind,
Nor the path to Spain have taken."
